entries.title: On a Windows PC, a running big build no longer holds its whole processor claim until it ends
entries.body: When a crewmate declares a big build or check, it waits in that computer's line until there is room. On a Windows PC a run that had started kept its whole declared processor count against the line until it finished. That reservation now ends at the first complete processor reading taken after the run's program started, as on a Mac or Linux computer. From then on the next run is judged by the processors the computer measures idle. It still waits for that reading, for enough idle processors and for enough memory.
entries.noPicture: A waiting run can start sooner; nothing on screen looks different while it waits or runs.
